🍄 Fomitopsidaceae / Agaricomycetes

ℹ️ Hymenium: Pores, initially yellow, maturing to brown or olive-brown, pores angular, 1–3 per mm
ℹ️ Cap: Typically fan-shaped or semicircular, surface velvety to woolly, ranging from yellow-brown to dark brown, often zoned with concentric bands of different colors
ℹ️ Hymenium Attachment: Decurrent, extending down the stipe
ℹ️ Stipe: Short, thick, and off-center, or sometimes absent; when present, the stipe is brown to dark brown and covered with a velvety texture similar to the cap
🟤 Spore print brownish
🪵🍂 Parasitic and saprobic, primarily found on the roots, lower trunks, and stumps of conifers, causes a brown cubical rot, late summer to autumn
🎨 Inedible, tough, and woody; used as a natural dye for fabrics rather than as food
📏 Fruit body large, 5 cm thick
📐 Cap 10–40 cm in diameter
👃 Odour mild to slightly unpleasant
🔬 Spores ellipsoid to cylindrical, 7–9 x 3–4 µm, smooth, hyphal structure is dimitic, with generative hyphae bearing clamps
🔤 Large, conspicuous fungus typically found growing on the roots and lower trunks of conifers
